### `cloud eval run`

Start an eval run of an existing suite, or upload a vers
ioned suite file and run it. Provide **either** `--suite` **or** `--file`, not both.\n\nBy default the command prints a launch rec
eipt and returns immediately. `--wait` polls every launched run to a terminal state.\n\n**Exit codes (`--wait` only).** Without `-
-wait` this command's exit code is unchanged: `0` on any launch, `1` on a partial or wholly failed fan-out. `--wait` owns a separa
te six-code contract; a caller who asked this process to sit and watch a run to completion is asking it to say how the run went:\n

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Every waited run passed, unanimously, and (when a report was requested) every report was
assembled |\n| `1` | A run **completed** with a **failed** verdict. The only condition that produces this code |\n| `2` | Usage er
ror: bad flags, `--reporter`/`--out` without `--wait`, or an invalid suite file (after auth, before any server/model work) |\n| `3
` | Auth failed: no credential, or the platform rejected it, at launch or mid-wait (a token that expired during a long poll). Zero
credits spent if it happened before launch |\n| `4` | Connection/setup failed before evaluation: a launch failure this CLI itself
observed (network, timeout, rate limit, a partial or failed fan-out, an unrecognized launch error), or a local `--out` write fail
ure, unless a more severe outcome (`1` or `3`) already applies to the same run, per the merge order above |\n| `5` | No valid verd
ict: `inconclusive`, a null/unrecognized result, a run whose own status is failed/cancelled/timed-out, a wait that hit its deadlin
e, a mid-wait failure that was not auth-shaped, or a report that could not be assembled |\n\nNo infrastructure condition ever maps
to `1`; see the same rule under `eval gate` below. A multi-target launch merges these worst-of across every waited run, in the or
der `1 > 3 > 4 > 5 > 0`: a real verdict failure is never masked by a sibling's infrastructure noise, and a credential failure (whi
ch may be *why* other targets show no verdict) outranks a plain connection failure.\n\nThis six-code contract is new and deliberat
ely **different** from `eval gate`'s four codes below; see that command's own doc for why the two are not unified. An invalid suit
e file exits **2** either way; `eval validate` still exits 1 for the same contract failure, because it is a verdict on the file an

d this command is not.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--suite <id-or-name>` | Yes, unless `--file` | Eval
suite name or ID |\n| `--file <path>` | Yes, unless `--suite` | Versioned suite file to upload and run (`.yaml` or `.json`, or `-
` for stdin) |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project) |\n| `--serve
r <id-or-name...>` | No | Override the suite's saved server selection (HTTP servers only) |\n| `--environment <id-or-name...>` | N
o | Attached project environment(s) to run. Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--client <id-or-name...>` | No | Att
ached client(s) to run, so the run is stamped with that client's config. Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--host
<id-or-name...>` | No | **Deprecated** alias for `--client`. Passing both is an error. Not the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam comp
at --host` / `mcpjam tools --host` take: see [Two different `--host` flags](#two-different---host-flags). |\n| `--all-targets` | N
o | Run **every** attached environment (or, if none, every attached host): one **paid run per target** |\n| `--iterations <n>` | N
o | Run each case this many times (1-10), for this run only |\n| `--repetitions <n>` | No | **Legacy** spelling of `--iterations`.
Passing both is an error. |\n| `--case <id-or-title...>` | No | Run only these cases instead of the whole suite |\n| `--refresh-s
napshot` | No | **Persists a new host-config snapshot on the suite** (see below). Single-target runs only. |\n| `--notes <text>` |
No | Free-text note stored on the run |\n| `--min-pass-rate <n>` | No | Pass threshold for this run (0-100), overriding the suite
's own |\n| `--match-options <json>` | No | Tool-call match options for this run, e.g. `'{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'` |\n| `--i
dempotency-key <key>` | No | Retry key for a lost launch response. For `--file`, a fresh key is minted and printed on every invoca
tion when this flag is omitted; supply the printed key to replay the same run instead of starting a new one |\n| `--wait` | No | W
ait for every launched run to reach a terminal status |\n| `--wait-timeout <ms>` | No | Maximum wait time (default 2100000); requi
res `--wait` |\n| `--reporter <json-summary\\|junit-xml\\|html>` | No | Write the completed structured report to stdout; requires
`--wait`. `html` is a self-contained decision summary + failures page: traces/parity/history are not included. |\n| `--out <path>`
| No | Atomically write the completed report to a file; defaults to `json-summary`, or uses `--reporter` when present; requires `
--wait` |\n| `--compose-client <id-or-name>` | No | Compose a stack to run instead of naming a saved environment (see below). **Ep
hemeral by default**: pass `--save-targets` to attach it to the suite. |\n| `--compose-host <id-or-name>` | No | **Deprecated** al
ias for `--compose-client` |\n| `--compose-model <id...>` | No | Model(s) to run on the composed stack. Replaces the client's pinn
ed model unless `--with-client-default` is set |\n| `--compose-model-selection <json...>` | No | Whole saved model selection(s) (s
ource, connection, `settings.reasoningEffort`) as JSON: one cell per selection, for its model, at its effort. Repeat to add severa
l selections for one model (e.g. at low and at high); each distinct selection is its own cell |\n| `--with-client-default` | No |
Also launch an inherit cell using each client's pinned model, alongside `--compose-model` |\n| `--compose-server <id-or-name...>`
| No | Server(s) to pin on the composed stack, snapshotted into a server group so a rerun keeps testing them. Mutually exclusive w
ith `--compose-server-group` |\n| `--compose-server-group <id>` | No | Standalone server group to pin on the composed stack |\n| `
--compose-host-servers` | No | **No longer supported**: rejected. An eval run takes its servers from a server group alone; use `--
compose-server` or `--compose-server-group` |\n| `--compose-secret <id...>` | No | Project secret IDs the composed stack grants to
its runs (`secrets list` shows them) |\n| `--save-targets` | No | Attach the composed environments to the suite (append, capped a

t 10). Without it the stack is ephemeral |
